# Download languages to use offline

Android phone & tabletiPhone & iPad

More

More

You can download languages onto your device. This lets you translate them without an internet connection.

After you’ve downloaded a language, you could be able to translate it by looking at it through your device's camera lens. [See languages that work with instant camera translations](https://support.google.com/translate/answer/6142483).

## Choose & download languages

1. Before you download languages, connect to Wi-Fi.
2. Open the Translate app ![Translate app](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/zbjy4lVco3DJT8GqHw3TXq74-q7utDszuEWMeKIpDcQTG-jL5v82cUTBy1wg=w16).
3. At the bottom, select the language you want to download.
4. Next to the language, tap Download ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/Xv_MeSheQLE6J9BLMqGbHnTNNxLUmILa3K4D2gfLbmyySjXzW3smBzecUdy6EP00I7w=w18).

   - If it’s not there, the language can’t be downloaded.
   - If it asks you to download the language file, tap **Download**.

**Tip:** In the Translate app, your saved languages show up as Downloaded ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/jpqh5kz_17k9ppEdam4C_65OOirxvrnMJ7vlqt36sw8O6VaiXcW6f6_f5DN9Yw=w18).

### Download languages without Wi-Fi

Since language files are small, when you’re not connected to Wi-Fi, you can download them with mobile data. If you don’t use Wi-Fi, it may affect your mobile carrier charges.

1. On your Android phone or tablet, open the Translate app ![Translate app](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/zbjy4lVco3DJT8GqHw3TXq74-q7utDszuEWMeKIpDcQTG-jL5v82cUTBy1wg=w16).
2. Tap Menu ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/UYVGdnOY33gkFyAvmY4Xa1Se8-bLinBEnU35eQ3kMlBrgHWj9g3AU6O-ekxOdxqkERk=w36-h36)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/QbWcYKta5vh_4-OgUeFmK-JOB0YgLLoGh69P478nE6mKdfpWQniiBabjF7FVoCVXI0g=h36) Settings ![Settings](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/357M8Fx_lLhnrWQd9imNXnB9lDqgu0a0t-9d6xzF1aU82S4S-3FBi86iLFjvieQkbV4Z=w36-h36)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/QbWcYKta5vh_4-OgUeFmK-JOB0YgLLoGh69P478nE6mKdfpWQniiBabjF7FVoCVXI0g=h36)**Data usage**.
3. Tap **Downloaded languages**.

   - **To always confirm before you download without Wi-Fi:** Tap **Ask before downloading**.
   - **To always use mobile data when you can't use Wi-Fi:** Tap **Use Wi-Fi or mobile network**.

## Update or remove languages

1. Connect to Wi-Fi.
2. On your Android phone or tablet, open the Translate app ![Translate app](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/zbjy4lVco3DJT8GqHw3TXq74-q7utDszuEWMeKIpDcQTG-jL5v82cUTBy1wg=w16).
3. Tap Menu ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/UYVGdnOY33gkFyAvmY4Xa1Se8-bLinBEnU35eQ3kMlBrgHWj9g3AU6O-ekxOdxqkERk=w36-h36)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/QbWcYKta5vh_4-OgUeFmK-JOB0YgLLoGh69P478nE6mKdfpWQniiBabjF7FVoCVXI0g=h36) Downloaded languages ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/ETm4UEMaQfHDOeP8aYuItPbd-4Q4hBq9kc2UZd2gAAEdYJm1jkYCSkV2-_p4K6mzMbkz=w36-h36).
4. You’ll get a list of available languages.
   - **To upgrade a language to a higher-quality language pack:** Next to the language, tap **Upgrade**.
   - **To update a language on your device:** Next to the language, tap **Update**.
   - **To delete a language from your device:** Tap Remove ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/omPP8k3T58rWn37iYHeqxPBOgiN6-8ILrPob4vuEdXX62w2a6efMb6114n-qQa06570=w36-h36). When asked if you want to remove the downloaded package, tap **Remove**.

# How can I get text to speech translations in offline mode?

I've downloaded the languages (french and arabic) to use them without needing internet, but I can only use the text to speech option with spanish (native language), so I was wondering if there is any option to download voice packages or something or that's managed by the phone.

Offline Speech output has never been supported directly by the Google Translate app. The Translate app itself does not download the data for Text To Speech (TTS) output.

I say "directly" because depending on your phone -- the text to speech system on your phone \*may\* work offline, depending on if it is Samsung TTS, Google/Pixel TTS, Motorola TTS, etc. When online, the Translate app requests TTS audio from Google servers. When offline, we fall back to the TTS as available on your particular phone, and whether the Android OS (not Google's) TTS service reports it can speak for a given language when offline. Depending on your phone's TTS setup (Samsung, Pixel, OnePlus, etc) -- TTS may work offline if your phone is so configured.

There is no ability for the Translate app to communicate or coordinate with each phone's TTS -- so offline TTS is hit-or-miss at this point. If you are able to download TTS offline in your phone's settings, then this may work, but Translate is unable to link you there or perform this configuration for you.

It's possible to include Google TTS with Translate, but the team is not in a position to develop such a feature at this time.

# Translate speech & text on your Pixel phone or Pixel Tablet

This article summarizes multiple translation features available on your device.

## Learn about Live Translate

**Important:** This feature is available on Pixel 6 and later.

You can detect and translate other languages on your phone with Live Translate.

- **Text and Apps:** Translate messages, on-screen text, and on-screen content. Translations for text and apps are available on Pixel 6 and later.
- **Phone calls:** Communicate in real-time with live voice translation. Translations for phone calls are available on Pixel 10 and later.
- **Media:** Get translated audio for videos, podcasts, and social media. Translations for media are available on Pixel 11 and later.

## Turn on Live Translate

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap **System**![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) **Live Translate**.
3. Turn on **Use Live Translate**.
4. To choose what’s translated, turn **Text**, **Phone Calls**, or **Media** on or off.

   - This setting is available for Pixel 11 series phones.
5. To add a language for Live Translate:
1. Tap **Add a language**.
2. Select a language to add.
3. Tap **Add language**.

**Tip:** You can add Live Translate to your Quick Settings menu.

### Use Live Translate for phone calls

**Important:**

- This feature is available on Pixel 10 and later.
- You can find this feature as “Voice Translate" on Pixel 10 series phones and as “Live Translate” on Pixel 11 series phones.

You can translate your voice into a selected language with Live Translate, and mimic your natural voice and tone in real-time.

To use Live Translate for calls:

1. Start a call.
2. Tap **Call Assist**.
3. To turn on live translation, tap **Live translate**.
4. Select the language the other party uses.
   - You can select your language and the speaker’s language
5. Tap **Done.**
   - You and the other party will each hear a brief announcement in your own language. Once it's complete, feel free to begin talking.

**Tips:**

- Live Translate can automatically detect when a spoken language has changed and prompt you to use the new language.
- Live Translate for phone calls is only available in certain countries and languages, and requires compatible apps. Translation accuracy may vary, so always double-check important information. [Learn how to use Live Translate for phone calls](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16477051).

## Use Live Translate for text messages

When you turn on Live Translate, you can translate text messages on some chat apps. All translations take place on your device. This feature is also available for Pixel Tablet.

To switch between the original and your chosen language, tap the language bubble.

To update language preferences:

1. Open a text conversation that’s in another language.
2. Tap the translate chip.
3. In the Drop-down ![Dropdown](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/uSM1WAyJPHhLEEJu9DClOxayx6mNNJ5pmlDbmNcokQTVVM2ZeN4QeoeVA2VX2IZ-Dg=w24), update the translation languages.

To translate a single message:

1. Open a text message that’s in another language.
2. Touch and hold to select text.
3. Tap Copy ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/_XIJRQWjEoyhUc-prh6jtMHSnTy4JgRRtZ5WX0kNwAiVE5MlpG98-LGJUa-SonuRB4ap=h36).
4. Tap **Translate copied text**.

**Tip:** To translate the full page, tap the Drop-down menu ![Dropdown](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/uSM1WAyJPHhLEEJu9DClOxayx6mNNJ5pmlDbmNcokQTVVM2ZeN4QeoeVA2VX2IZ-Dg=w24)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36)**Translate full page**.

## Use Live Translate for media

**Important:**

- This feature is available on Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
- This feature is available for certain apps, such as YouTube and select third-party apps.

You can translate audio and video from select apps in real time with Live Translate for media. It allows you to listen to media in your chosen language by translating the audio on your device.

To use Live Translate for media:

1. Play media.
2. At the top of the screen, tap the on-screen button that appears.
3. To translate your media, select the language you want to translate into.

**Tip:** This feature works best with a clear primary speaker and low background noise. It doesn’t translate music.

## Other translation features

### Translate text with your camera

You can translate text using your camera.

1. On your Pixel search bar, tap Lens ![Google Lens](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/_CvuGn9oD10CLj9B_bsCXxBaRbUGdaU_WJhKdjxTdcnFx9PopQygjB2ImtWEwyUB1Gg=w36-h36).
2. Take a photo of the text you want to translate.

### Translate as you scroll with Circle to Search

You can translate webpages and apps as you scroll. [Learn how to use Circle to Search on your Pixel phone or tablet](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/14542478).

To translate as you scroll down a page or switch apps:

1. Touch and hold the **Home button** or navigation bar at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap Translate ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/1jWYmAFcMBdGaYjrudVScZc_VJYeFTQH4rGaLiX9Tf4MVETsVNKhgTBitikHHCi4SA=h36)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) Scroll and translate ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/hrHmOv_CTGgOebJH6pTW4fzyxS2K7kNTi8IXpzwjyEyJaAj4KTQexGTZzE0NutWZGjI=h36).

Translation works for most content types like webpages, messages, and social media, but not videos and GIFs.

### Translate captions on media

You can switch caption languages on media like videos, podcasts, phone calls, video calls, and audio messages. [Learn more about Live Caption](https://support.google.com/accessibility/android/answer/9350862?hl=en).

## Use Google Translate with Dual Screen support (Pixel Fold (1st Gen) and later)

You can use Google Translate for a more natural way to translate, which makes face-to-face conversations in different languages even easier. With Dual Screen support, translations appear on the inside and outside screens.

**Important:** To make sure that the translation is correct when you use Dual Screen, make sure you don't cover the microphone.

To use Dual Screen in Google Translate:

1. Open your Google Translate app ![Translate app](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/ZlZl5FCNSoJ8or5fREg43T6t9kdo02nLL2IXugtH7iOv-ZJ2L4rxByIkw3NCYi8-7Ks=w36-h36).
2. Unfold your phone.
3. Click **Conversation**.
4. Tap Face to face ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/Agg26eGj3eBovbxX5wt7INXGiVjmGMp4CnaIEtYr0kOWDdinoqLrc6IaRxUqV54t_sY=h36).
5. Tap Dual Screen ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/oK0kNJ60m_jVEGg3BGIzwZPd8CInRDzkCqWTc-lVG2iFqkGYsZnKqhdLFhR5ACcMt60=h36).
6. Start speaking and the translation will appear on the outer screen.

[Skip to main content](https://support.google.com/googlepixelbuds/answer/7573100?hl=en#hcfe-content) # Translate with Google Pixel Buds Google Pixel Buds help you translate easily with your Pixel or compatible Android phone. Follow conversations in real-time using Face-to-Face Live Translate mode, or use Explorer Mode to automatically translate ambient sounds. To use with Google Translate, make sure you have: - The Google Pixel Buds connected to your phone. - [A Gemini compatible Android device](https://support.google.com/assistant/answer/7172657?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en) (The device must meet all requirements within the linked article). - [Gemini as your default voice assistant](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14554984), with Live Translate permissions turned on. - [The latest version of the Google app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox&hl=en). - [The latest version of the Google Translate app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.translate). - An internet connection. Google Translate works with all Gemini-optimized headphones and Android phones. Gemini on Pixel Buds requires: - A Gemini-enabled device with Android version 6.0 or higher. - A Google Account. - An internet connection. Data rates may apply. For minimum requirements, go to [Get help from Google Assistant on Google Pixel Buds](https://support.google.com/googlepixelbuds/answer/7560032). ## Use Live Translate straight from your Pixel Buds - **Listening mode:** Once set up, you can press and hold on your buds to instantly launch the Google Translate app in listening mode - or just ask Gemini “Hey Google, translate for me”. This enables you to continuously translate spoken language as you navigate an environment, streaming the translated audio directly into your ear. All hands free - leaving your phone in your pocket. - **Conversation mode:** Start a conversation session enhanced with automatic Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) to optimize your discussion. Your speech plays aloud through your phone's speaker, while the other person's translated speech plays privately directly in your earbud. Supported languages With the Google Translate app on your phone, your Google Pixel Buds can translate conversations between the following languages: | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Afrikaans | English | Japanese | Serbian | | Arabic | Finnish | Khmer | Sinhala | | Armenian | French | Korean | Slovak | | Bengali | German | Latvian | Spanish | | Catalan | Greek | Nepali | Swahili | | Chinese
(Mandarin only) | Hindi | Norwegian | Swedish | | Croatian | Hungarian | Polish | Tamil | | Czech | Icelandic | Portuguese | Thai | | Danish | Indonesian | Romanian | Turkish | | Dutch | Italian | Russian | Vietnamese | ### Using Live Translate on Pixel Buds in Listening Mode **Important:** You can’t use Gemini commands during an active translation session. #### Control your active Live Translate sessions with your voice assistant 1. Say "Hey Google, start translating" to activate your voice assistant. 2. This launches the Google Translate app on your phone in listening mode. You can move around and have voices you hear be automatically translated into your ear. 3. Double tap when done. #### Control your active Live Translate sessions with gestures During setup, you can customize your earbud gestures to launch Live Translate. - **Single tap:** Pauses or resumes translation. - **Double tap:** Exits the session. - **Remove one Bud:** Translation continues. (No impact) - **Remove both Buds:** Translation exits. [Learn more about using the Google Translate App](https://support.google.com/translate/answer/6142474?hl=en&ref_topic=7011659&sjid=7319581387466120537-NC&co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&oco=1). ## Switch to Conversation Mode When you want to have a conversation with someone and need two way translation, so they can understand you as well as you can understand them, then you can seamlessly switch to conversation mode. 1. Pull out your phone and open up the translation app. 2. If you are already in listening mode, you can tap “listening mode” to switch modes to conversation Mode. Otherwise, just tap on live translate ![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) conversation mode Once in conversation mode, your voice will be translated and shown on the phone (and optionally played out loud) while the other person’s voice will be translated and played in your ear. With Google Assistant #### Step 1: Ask Google Assistant to help transcribe with Google Pixel Buds 1. While you're wearing Pixel Buds, press and hold either earbud or say, "Hey Google." 2. Request assistance, such as "Ayúdame a entender inglés." This launches Google Translate in transcribe mode listening to the language you request (English) and translating to your default language (French, German, Italian or Spanish). Assistant queries for transcribe mode French: Hey Google, aide-moi à comprendre l'anglais. German: Hey Google, hilf mir, Englisch zu verstehen. Italian: Hey Google, aiutami a capire l'inglese. Spanish: Hey Google, ayúdame a entender inglés. #### Step 2: Begin listening Listen through your Pixel Buds along with the transcript on your phone. The text is read aloud after each sentence is translated. Without Google Assistant #### Step 1: Select your languages 1. Open Translate ![Translate app](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/ZlZl5FCNSoJ8or5fREg43T6t9kdo02nLL2IXugtH7iOv-ZJ2L4rxByIkw3NCYi8-7Ks=w36-h36). 2. Tap microphone ![Voice](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/rm6250W327ewIJ6iZh1mJQCOCZjNK_djptXOc8C3UGpkIs5zLNs429KleTctU9hI-C7b=w36-h36)![and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) Transcribe ![Transcribe](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/s21uHRjUaYkzZgFQuoRYWAZHr01XzZzSEc48GlEyrT1ATrJFmvKEAfl41hvQlEN1hQ=w36). 3. At the bottom left corner, select the language you want to listen to (supported language: English). 4. At the bottom right corner, select the language with the spoken words to be translated into (supported languages: French, German, Italian or Spanish). #### Step 2: Begin listening Listen through your Pixel Buds along with the transcript on your phone. The text is read aloud after each sentence is translated. ## Tips and troubleshooting To get the best results, make sure to: - Move closer to the audio source. - Ask the speaker to talk louder, slower, or more clearly. - Switch the microphone on and off. - Check that your input or output languages are correct. - Verify your Wi-Fi connection. - Ensure necessary language packs are [downloaded for uninterrupted offline translation](https://support.google.com/translate/answer/6142473). Requires a Google Assistant-enabled Android 6.0+ device, Google Account, and an internet connection. Data rates may apply. Translation isn't instantaneous. Hi,

Here are some of the troubleshooting steps to fix this kind of issues.

﻿ 1\. Ensure the your language pack is fully downloaded:

\- Go to the Google Translate app on your device.

\- Tap on the "Settings" icon (gear icon).

\- Select "Offline translation."

\- Check if the your language pack is listed as "Available for offline use" and indicates a downloaded size.

\- If it's not downloaded, tap "Download" next to the your language.

2\. Confirm Your Offline Mode:

\- Ensure your device is in Airplane Mode or completely disconnected from the internet.

\- Turn off Wi-Fi and cellular data connections.

3\. Restart the Google Translate App:

\- Close the Google Translate app completely.

\- Relaunch the app and check if it now works offline.

4\. Check App Permissions:

\- Make sure the Google Translate app has the necessary permissions, such as storage access and internet access, enabled.

\- Go to your device's "Settings" > "Apps" or "Application Manager."

\- Find the Google Translate app and select "Permissions."

\- Enable all the necessary permissions, including storage and internet access.

5\. Reinstall the Google Translate App:

\- If the issue persists, try reinstalling the Google Translate app.

\- Uninstall the app from your device.

\- Restart your device.

\- Download and reinstall the Google Translate app from the App Store or Google Play Store.

﻿ 1\. Ensure the your language pack is fully downloaded:

\- Go to the Google Translate app on your device.

\- Tap on the "Settings" icon (gear icon).

\- Select "Offline translation."

\- Check if the your language pack is listed as "Available for offline use" and indicates a downloaded size.

\- If it's not downloaded, tap "Download" next to the your language.

2\. Confirm Your Offline Mode:

\- Ensure your device is in Airplane Mode or completely disconnected from the internet.

\- Turn off Wi-Fi and cellular data connections.

3\. Restart the Google Translate App:

\- Close the Google Translate app completely.

\- Relaunch the app and check if it now works offline.

4\. Check App Permissions:

\- Make sure the Google Translate app has the necessary permissions, such as storage access and internet access, enabled.

\- Go to your device's "Settings" > "Apps" or "Application Manager."

\- Find the Google Translate app and select "Permissions."

\- Enable all the necessary permissions, including storage and internet access.

5\. Reinstall the Google Translate App:

\- If the issue persists, try reinstalling the Google Translate app.

\- Uninstall the app from your device.

\- Restart your device.

\- Download and reinstall the Google Translate app from the App Store or Google Play Store.
